title: What's New in SearchDeadCode
tagline: Dead code across the whole workspace, in one pass
summary: The first release brings the searchdeadcode CLI into the editor: one command sweeps the workspace, and every finding lands in the Problems panel where you already work.

highlights.title: One Command, Whole Workspace
highlights.description: "Scan for dead code" runs the analyzer over every Kotlin and Java file and reports what nothing reaches: unused declarations, dead parameters, orphaned resources.

highlights.title: No CLI Install Needed
highlights.description: Platform builds ship the analyzer inside the extension. Nothing to install, nothing to put on PATH. Point at your own build through searchdeadcode.path if you prefer.

highlights.title: Silence a Finding Without Deleting It
highlights.description: Not every finding should go. Add one to the baseline file, or drop an inline ignore that records why the declaration has to stay. Raise searchdeadcode.minConfidence to see only what the analyzer can prove.

sections.title: Getting Started
sections.body: Open a Kotlin or Java project and run "Scan for dead code (workspace)" from the command palette. Findings appear in the Problems panel; "Clear dead code findings" empties it.

sections.title: Requirements
sections.body: The analyzer runs as a local process, so the extension needs a desktop VS Code. It is not available on vscode.dev.
